## What it is

A physically proven print-in-place collar for the joint between two recording masts. Its smooth bore slides into position freely; a D-shaped cam turns to press both mast segments against the opposite wall.

## Design notes

The 44 mm collar grips 22 mm above and below the mast seam. Its normal opening is 24.2 x 18.2 mm, with no internal pressure bands. A vertical D-shaped cam runs through a reinforced boss on the front face. In the printed position the cam's flat faces the mast and clears it by 0.35 mm. Turning the finger tab a quarter-turn presents the round face and produces 0.15 mm nominal pressure.

The rotating member is a 5.4 mm D-shaped cam inside a 6.1 mm straight-through bearing. Its flat side provides 0.35 mm mast clearance in the printed position; presenting the round side adds the 0.15 mm squeeze. A vertical finger tab shows the flat's direction. Two 0.6 x 0.5 mm breakaway bridges connect the cam to the housing during printing so the STL remains one object. After printing, support the collar and push the bottom of the cam upward with a blunt 2–3 mm rod or Allen key; this shears the bridges without bending the finger tab. Reseat the cam, verify that it rotates freely, and only then fit the collar to a mast. The checker sees the deliberate 0.35 mm air gap as one thin section and the bridge/cam junctions as fourteen small faces; these are confined to the moving release mechanism, not structural walls.

Print upright, exactly as modelled, without supports. Physical testing on the Kobra S1 confirmed that the release clearance works and the quarter-turn cam holds the mast nicely once released and understood. The quarter-turn direction can be chosen by feel: turn until the mast is held firmly, without forcing the tab beyond its comfortable stop. Print two for the complete stand.

## Don't

Do not twist harder if the finger tab itself bends; push the cam upward from below to shear the release bridges. Do not lubricate or sand the cam before its first movement test; that would hide whether the 0.35 mm print-in-place clearance works on this printer. The cam is retained by gravity during normal upright use but can deliberately be lifted out for cleaning; do not mistake that serviceability for a failed print. Do not increase the physically proven cam pressure. Keep the simpler friction-band collar as a no-moving-parts fallback.
